content.title: 30 April Fools’ Day Pranks That Are Silly, Sweet, and Totally Kid-Approved
content.text: Whether you are a family of seasoned pranksters or occasional comedians, a well-planned gag will surely score some chuckles this April Fools' Day. But planning the perfect prank is no simple feat. The key is understanding your audience and thinking outside the box—which may mean saying goodbye to predictable prank calls and worn-out whoopee cushions. For some memorable prank inspiration, here are 30 April Fools' Day pranks that are wholesome enough for the whole family. Dough…Not For older kids who may not be totally devastated by a sweet treat switch-up, try your hand at transforming an apple into a decadent donut with these simple instructions: Peel and core an apple, then cut it in half horizontally.Next, use a knife to trim the bottom, so it's curved (like a doughnut).Melt 6 ounces of candy melts (vanilla or chocolate will work, as this will serve as your "frosting").Pat the apple dry.Dip the apples top-down into the candy melts, set them on wax paper, and cover them with sprinkles. The good news about this prank is that candy-coated apple slices are just as delicious as a donut—and your kids will get some fiber, too! Cereal Surprise Hide realistic-looking gummy worms in the bottom of your kid's cereal bowl for an "eww"-worthy breakfast prank. Just be sure they're not too tempted to eat only gummy worms for breakfast! Pop Goes the Carpet Everyone loves a good piece of bubble wrap, but in this prank, you can put your leftover bubble wrap to good use by having your child "pop" in for a surprise. To pull off the bubble wrap prank, cut a piece of large bubble wrap (aka the big bubble kind!) to fit under your child's rug. Hide it before they get up. If it's a larger rug, slip a piece under where they'll step. Wait to hear giggles when the rug goes "pop!" If your child doesn't have a rug in their room, you could also try hiding bubble wrap in other places in your home, like under a cushion on a chair, in their shoe, or another common area rug where they may step. Maybe a little special after-shower surprise? Meatloaf Surprise Here's an unforgettable April Fools' prank for kids: Make meatloaf and mashed potatoes look like a decadent cake! Here's how: Divide 3 pounds of your favorite meatloaf recipe into two 8-inch round cake pans and bake (drain off any liquid that remains in the pan).You'll need 5 to 6 cups of smooth mashed potatoes to frost the layers.Use a pastry bag and tip to pipe on additional mashed spuds for an extra-convincing confection. Not only does this fun dinner make for a great April Fools' prank, but it will also get some healthy nutrients, like protein and veggies, into the meal as well. Help! My Screen Broke! This is a perfect last-minute April Fools' Day prank. Start by downloading a realistic image of a broken phone screen. Then, pretend to drop your phone and act devastated, showing your family the image of the broken screen. Good Morning Gag This prank only works when April Fools' Day falls on a weekend since it involves tricking your kids into thinking it's a school day. Have them wake up and get ready as usual. Up the ante by making sure you're "running late." Say: "We're going to miss the bus! I'll have to drive you." Then, instead of pulling up to school, take them to their fave breakfast spot. If your kids are too old to pull this prank off, you could also consider changing the clocks so you have an extra hour to surprise them with a quick breakfast or muffin run before school, too! Faux Cookie Dough Dip This deceptively delicious recipe has the texture and flavor of homemade cookie dough, but it's actually a bean dip in disguise. Here's the recipe: In a food processor, blend 1 1/2 cups chickpeas, 6 tablespoons brown sugar, 1/4 cup peanut butter, 3 tablespoons oats, 1 tablespoon milk, 2 teaspoons vanilla, and 1/8 teaspoon each salt and baking soda.Fold in 1/3 cup of chocolate chips.Serve with apple slices or other fresh fruit. If you ask us, this isn't even a prank you'd need to feel bad about, because it's healthy and delicious! But it might garner some interesting reactions when you "spill the beans" to your kids about what ingredients are actually in the dip. Green Water Make green water pour out of the bathroom faucet by using a Q-tip to put green food dye under the faucet spout. When your kids turn the sink on, the water will run green! Charcuterie Change-Up For an afternoon snack they won't expect, make a meat and cheese board with two secret kid-favorite ingredients: cookies and candy! The cookies and candy chews stand in for the traditional savory snacks. Here's how to pull this prank off: To make the crackers, pull apart several vanilla sandwich cookies. Leave the filling intact and scatter green sugar sprinkles on half the pieces. Scrape away any filling from the others.For the cheese, soften white and orange fruit chews (we used Tootsie Fruit Rolls) in the microwave for a few seconds, then shape them into cubes or roll the candy flat and use a knife to trim it into rectangles. Form the holes with a small cookie cutter or piping tip. Honk Honk Leave a note on your car saying, "Honk and wave, I'm playing an April Fool's joke on my kids." Your kids will be shocked when the commute to school is full of everyone honking and waving at you. Micro Meal This April Fool's prank, while small in proportions, will generate big belly laughs! Here's how to present your kids with a miniature lunch: Line a small empty matchbox with foil or parchment paper (so that the food can be eaten, if desired).With a glue stick, attach a 2- by 4-inch piece of decorative paper around the exterior.For the handle, squeeze a drop of tacky glue onto each end of a 1-inch length of pipe cleaner and adhere it to one side of the box.Finally, pack it with a teensy lunch. Not sure what to pack? Try these fun miniature-sized ideas: Sandwich: With a sharp knife, cut little triangles of bread, lunch meat, and lettuce, then stack them.Doughnut: Frost the top of an O-shaped cereal piece and sprinkle it with nonpareils.Carrot: Slice a bit of carrot into miniature carrot sticks.Raisins: Chop a raisin into tiny pieces. A Sticky Surprise This is a great last-minute idea if you have post-it notes lying around. Take post-it notes and draw faces on them, leave them all over the house (including mirrors!) for your family to find. The Colossal Popsicle So your kid has a huge appetite for frozen treats? Wow them with a giant ice pop that's as big as their head! To make a simple version: Remove the top from a 46-ounce can of juice, pour out a little of the juice (so it won't overflow when it freezes), and insert a foot-long length of 1-inch wooden dowel.Place strips of masking tape across the can to hold the dowel in place, then place the can in the freezer overnight or until the juice is solid.To remove the pop, run the can under hot water to loosen it. After the prank is played, chop up the pop and put the pieces in a blender or food processor to make delicious shaved ice (that can be served in more reasonably sized portions). Trick Treats Remove the wrappers from Tootsie Rolls and replace the candy with cut and peeled carrot pieces. For individually wrapped bubble gum, use cut sections of string cheese. Just be sure your child is old enough to handle those unexpected carrot pieces—choking hazards will never be funny! Broken Funny Bone What kid hasn't secretly longed to show up for school with a broken limb so they can bask in the attention and collect the loving signatures of well-wishers? This prank allows kids to cast themselves in that starring role without suffering. As a bonus, this reusable fake is a fun prop to keep around for make-believe health care provider visits. Start by gathering the supplies: One knee-high white tube sockPaper-towel tubePlastic grocery bagsMasking tapePlastic wrapFoam brushWhite glue Then follow the instructions below. Cut the toe off the sock, then make a thumb hole by cutting a half-inch slit an inch from the cut end.To make a cast form, bulk up a paper towel tube by wrapping three or four plastic bags around it. Secure them with masking tape. Cover the form in plastic wrap, then slide on the sock. Attach a length of masking tape down the sock.Use the foam brush to apply a thick layer of glue all over the sock, except where the masking tape is (this unglued area will allow the cast to stretch so that the wearer can easily slip it on and off). Let the sock dry overnight. Remove the masking tape, then remove the cast from the form. Your family can sign the "cast" with markers at home. Cracked TV Screen This one is a classic. While your family is away, cast a broken video screen video from YouTube. Watch as all the screen-time lovers in your family panic as they "realize" the TV screen is broken. Playing Chicken For a wacky stunt on April Fools' Day, deck your family's helmets with some chicken-inspired trimmings, then get ready to hear some chuckling—and possibly some clucking—as you cruise the neighborhood. Here's what you'll need: FeltTacky glueLarge googly eyesOld socksCotton batting or other stuffingSafety pinsHeavy-duty double-sided tapePair of glovesEmbroidery threadLarge-eyed needle To make, follow these instructions: Cut a figure-eight shape from the felt. Glue on the googly eyes.To make the nose, cut off the toe of the sock and stuff it. Using a safety pin, attach it to the felt. Adhere the felt to the back of the helmet with double-sided tape.Stuff the gloves, tucking in the cuffs to hold the stuffing in place. With the double-sided tape, adhere the gloves to the top of the helmet.Using the embroidery thread and needle, make a few stitches through each glove and knot the thread ends inside the helmet. Cookie Swap Everyone loves a good cookie swap, right? Only, this cookie swap may surprise your kids with a bit more than they bargained for. Take some Oreo cookies, or any store-brand cookie with a white filling, and gently twist the tops off. Scrape the filling off with a knife, then replace the filling with toothpaste, mashed potatoes, or another unexpected white filling. Fasten the cookie tops back on and serve up a surprise! Bugging Out One of our favorite easy pranks for kids is to get some plastic bugs (we're partial to realistic cockroaches, but any bug will work) and hide them in a spot your kid visits every day, like their shoe or pillow. Listen for a squeal and know that your prank was a success! Auto-Correction For older kids who may have phones, sneak in when they're not using their devices and set a commonly used phrase or word to auto-correct to something else. Maybe switch up their "idk" or "idc" to "I LOVE MOM" or "I'd love to do the dishes tonight, don't worry." Sounds like the best April Fool's ever! Clean-up Time This prank is great if you have wooden floors or an outdoor space. All you need is a cup and a thick card. First, fill the cup with water, then place a thick card over the cup. Next, quickly flip the cup over and set it on the table without spilling the water. The card should hold the water in place. Leave a note instructing the finder to clean up the mess! Try a Sip From This Cup This April Fools' Day prank will need to be prepared the night before. You'll need two clear glasses and Jello mix. Start by making the Jello and putting the mix into the glasses, insert a straw before putting the glasses in the fridge to set. The next day (on April 1), take the glasses out and pretend like it's a glass of juice, serve it to your kids alongside a plate of food and wait for them to take a sip from the straw! Pro Tip: When placing the glasses in the fridge to set, hide them behind something your kids will never touch so the secret isn't spoiled. Endless Underwear For this April Fools' Day prank, you'll need a long string and a needle. Start by going to your child's room and gathering a bunch of their underwear. Then, sew all of their underwear together into one long chain and put it back as it was before, hiding that it is all sown together. When your child goes to put a pair on, they'll be shocked that all their underwear is connected together. The Frozen Bowl Make your kids a bowl of fruit the night before and put it in the freezer to freeze. On April Fools' Day, give them the bowl as a snack, they'll be surprised when they can't pull apart each piece because it's frozen together! Hidden Alarm This one is great if you have a teen with their own phone. Set an alarm on their phone for the middle of the night and hide the phone somewhere in their room. When they wake, they'll scramble to look for their phone to shut off the alarm. I Stepped In... For all the families with dogs, this one is for you. Take your dog on a walk and bring a jar of peanut butter or hazelnut spread. Before coming back inside, smear some on the bottom of your shoe. Tell your family you stepped on the dog's poop, then smell it and take a tiny taste from the top of the blob. Your family will look shocked as they watch you enjoy what they believe is dog poop. Get Your Greens Take lollipop and remove the candy from the stem, replace it with a single Brussels sprout and put the wrapper back on to hide the surprise. Pass Me the Toilet Paper, Please! For this April Fools' Day prank, start by bringing melted chocolate into the bathroom. Pretend like you're going to the bathroom and then ask your child to bring you a roll of toilet paper. Before they arrive, place melted chocolate on your fingers. When they pass you the roll, smear the chocolate all over their hand. They'll be entirely grossed out at the thought that something else got on them. Brown “E’s” Print out a bunch of brown letter "E's" from the internet and cut them out. On April 1, take a baking dish and place all the brown E's on a baking dish. Tell your kids that you've made brownies and they should come try them. Whoopee! Last, but certainly not least, is the beloved prank classic—the whoopee cushion. Take a whoopee cushion and put it just about anywhere your family is about to sit down and wait to hear the fart noise. They'll be surprised and everyone is sure to have a laugh. Related Stories
